title: The uncle, Tuesday
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday, before the shop. Seven AM. The uncle already in the chair. Wood draws him from the dock's end, far, the chair small, the shack, the pots. The uncle asks why so far. Wood says to get the shack in. The uncle says the shack'll keep.

panels.composition: The launch at seven from the dock's end: the shack, the pots on the wall, the chair, the UNCLE small in it. WOOD at the dock's end with the pad. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a boat launch at early morning seen from the end of a dock with a shingle shack, a wall of crab pots and a small figure in a lawn chair, a young man drawing at the dock's end, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the whole launch. The uncle a few strokes. The shack most of it.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a wide drawing of a boat launch and shack where an old man in a chair is a few small strokes, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle, calling down the dock.

image.prompt: an old man in a lawn chair calling toward a dock, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood walking back up the dock. Sitting on the pot. Close. Drawing again. Tuesday. The shack'll keep.

image.prompt: a young man walking up a dock to sit close beside an old man in a lawn chair and draw again, black and white, no words
